_meta.indication: VIMPAT (lacosamide) tablets are indicated as adjunctive therapy in the treatment of partial-onset seizures in patients with epilepsy aged 17 years and older; the injection is indicated as adjunctive therapy when oral administration is temporarily not feasible

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multicenter (US and Europe), double-blind, parallel-group trial; patients on 1 or 2 AEDs randomized to lacosamide 200, 400, or 600 mg/day or placebo, with 8-week baseline, 6-week titration, and 12-week maintenance phases
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with uncontrolled partial-onset seizures taking 1 or 2 concomitant AEDs
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Reduction from baseline in 4-week seizure frequency during the Maintenance Phase
pivotal_trials.result: Median percent reduction in seizure frequency vs placebo: 200 mg/day -14.8% (p=0.14), 400 mg/day -27.9% (p=0.003), 600 mg/day -21.5% (p=0.026)

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Design similar to Study 667, with 3 groups (placebo, 400, and 600 mg/day), conducted entirely in the US
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with uncontrolled partial-onset seizures taking concomitant AEDs
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Reduction from baseline in 4-week seizure frequency during the Maintenance Phase
pivotal_trials.result: Median percent reduction in seizure frequency vs placebo: 400 mg/day -21.2% (p=0.011), 600 mg/day -24.8% (p=0.009)

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Design similar to the other two studies, with 3 arms (placebo, 200 mg/day, and 400 mg/day), performed in Europe and Australia, with a 4-week titration phase
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with uncontrolled partial-onset seizures taking concomitant AEDs
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Reduction from baseline in 4-week seizure frequency during the Maintenance Phase
pivotal_trials.result: Median percent reduction in seizure frequency vs placebo: 200 mg/day -13.6% (p=0.05), 400 mg/day -27.3% (p=0.027)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=2% and more frequent than placebo) in partial-onset seizure trials included dizziness (31% VIMPAT total vs 8% placebo), headache (13% vs 9%), diplopia (11% vs 2%), and nausea (11% vs 4%); dizziness was the most frequent AE leading to discontinuation (3%)
target_moa: Antiepileptic drug whose precise mechanism is not fully elucidated; lacosamide selectively enhances slow inactivation of voltage-gated sodium channels, stabilizing hyperexcitable neuronal membranes and inhibiting repetitive neuronal firing, and also binds CRMP-2

rems.type: A REMS consisting of a Medication Guide and a timetable for submission of REMS assessments was approved; FDA determined that Vimpat poses a serious and significant public health concern requiring distribution of a Medication Guide

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened because the products are members of the previously approved class of anti-epileptic drugs and did not pose unique concerns

description.text: Eliminated the REMS requirement for Vimpat (lacosamide)

citations.quote: This supplemental new drug application proposes to eliminate the requirement for the approved Vimpat (lacosamide) REMS.

description.text: Revised labeling to update Section 10.1 to include postmarketing overdose experience and clarify clinical overdose description

citations.quote: These “Changes Being Effected” supplemental new drug applications provide for revised labeling to update Section 10.1 to include postmarketing overdose experience and to make minor clarifications to the clinical overdose experience description.

description.text: Expanded treatment of partial-onset seizures to include pediatric patients 4 years of age and older (previously adults only)

citations.quote: VIMPAT is indicated for the treatment of partial-onset seizures in patients 4 years of age and older.

basis.text: The application was reviewed under a Standard review priority

summary.text: VIMPAT was approved via a standard (non-priority) full approval as adjunctive therapy for partial-onset seizures in adults, based on three adequate and well-controlled trials; no advisory committee was convened, a Medication Guide REMS was required, and pediatric studies were deferred as a postmarketing requirement

citations.quote: The sponsor has submitted adequate evidence of safety and substantial evidence of effectiveness for the use of lacosamide oral tablets as adjunctive treatment for partial seizures in adults with epilepsy.

Your applications for Vimpat (lacosamide) Tablets and Injection (NDA 22-253, 22-254) were not referred to an FDA advisory committee because your products are members of the class of previously approved anti-epileptic drugs and the products did not pose unique concerns beyond those applicable to other members of this class.

requirement.text: Deferred pediatric studies under PREA for the adjunctive treatment of partial onset seizures in pediatric patients ages 1 month up to 17 years (final report submission July 2013)

citations.quote: Deferred pediatric studies under PREA for the adjunctive treatment of partial onset seizures in pediatric patients ages 1 month up to 17 years.

requirement.text: A nonclinical study in rats under 505(o)(3) to examine effects of Vimpat on brain development during the prenatal and early postnatal periods using more sensitive techniques for assessing CNS structure and function

citations.quote: A nonclinical study in rats to examine the effects of Vimpat (lacosamide) on brain development during the prenatal and early postnatal periods using more sensitive techniques for assessing central nervous system structure and function than were employed in the standard pre- and postnatal development study.

requirement.text: In vitro data to determine which enzymes, in addition to CYP2C19, may be involved in the metabolism of Vimpat (lacosamide) (final report within 18 months of approval)
